problems.title: Correct stationary limit and a graph-level counterexample
problems.source_location: Main PDF p.4, Section 2.2, Theorem 1, Eqs 1-2 Main PDF p.5, Section 3.2
claim: Theorem 1 identifies the deep symmetric-normalized propagation limit with an arithmetic-mean projector and uses it to infer graph-level collapse.
analysis: For a connected aperiodic graph with augmented degrees \(\widetilde d_i\), the normalized adjacency power converges to \(uu^\top\), where \(u_i=\sqrt{\widetilde d_i}/\sqrt{\sum_j\widetilde d_j}\). For the self-looped three-node path, \(u=(\sqrt2,\sqrt3,\sqrt2)/\sqrt7\), which is not the uniform vector. Thus \(uu^\top\ne\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top/3\). In the paper's linear identity-weight setting, equal initial features on this path and a regular triangle need not have equal limiting mean readouts: degree factors remain. The arithmetic-mean limit and the resulting universal graph-level conclusion therefore fail.

With constant scalar initial node feature \(1\), the self-looped path has limiting mean readout \((11+4\sqrt6)/21\), while the self-looped regular triangle has limiting mean \(1\). Their equal initial feature means therefore do not imply equal limiting graph readouts under the theorem’s own linear identity-weight simplification.
result: The counterexample refutes the stated stationary identity and graph-level implication. It does not deny empirical oversmoothing in graph networks.
repair: Use the degree-dependent projector and specify conditions on limiting graph readouts. Distinguish mean/sum pooling, regular/disconnected graphs, weights and nonlinearities.
problems.impact_rationale: The exact limiting projector underpinning the core oversmoothing argument is wrong on a simple admissible graph.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: Smaller spectral radius does not establish anti-collapse
problems.source_location: Main PDF p.7, Section 4, Eqs 11-12 and following paragraph
claim: Section 4 treats a reduced spectral radius as sufficient evidence against collapse.
analysis: Admissible equal two-view gates produce \(M=S/2\), with spectral radius \(1/2\). If \(S^L\to uu^\top\), then \(M^L=2^{-L}S^L\to0\): features collapse to zero. Relative eigenvalue ratios are unchanged by this scalar rescaling, so normalized oversmoothing is not removed either.
result: Reducing the absolute spectral radius does not establish the claimed anti-collapse property. Learned gates and nonlinearities need their own analysis; classifier accuracy is not determined by this linear example.
repair: Analyze relative spectral decay under the actual recurrence. A qualified linear remedy is persistent initial-feature injection with convergent resolvent; its assumptions and effect on accuracy would still require verification.
problems.impact_rationale: An admissible gated propagation has the advertised smaller spectral radius while collapsing to zero, directly contradicting the core anti-collapse inference.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: Evaluation-time BatchNorm and node-order dependence
claim: The graph classifier's evaluation should respect node relabeling and its stated normalization convention.
analysis: Fresh BatchNorm1d uses node index as channel and remains training-mode even after parent.eval(); it is unregistered and called unconditionally once. Helper batch-change error \(2.15487\); five full-model seeds produce relabeling differences \(0.000326\)–\(0.007388\).
result: Symmetric full-model input yielded only \(1.19\times10^{-7}\) relabeling difference; that negative result is retained. Synthetic differences are not benchmark accuracy changes.
repair: Use registered, appropriately masked feature normalization or per-node LayerNorm; preserve evaluation mode and node equivariance.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: Parameter registration can be lost on device transfer
claim: The learned convolution parameters must remain registered after device placement.
analysis: nn.Parameter(cpu_tensor).to(device) returns an ordinary non-leaf Tensor when a device copy occurs, losing module parameter registration. Actual GraphConv has weight/bias on CPU but no named parameters on meta device.
result: CUDA execution was not performed. A no-op CPU conversion can conceal the issue; no inference about undisclosed historical training is made.
repair: Create tensors on the target device before wrapping, or move the completed module. Check named_parameters, state_dict and optimizer membership; retrain after repair.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: Padding is treated as graph content
claim: Zero padding should not become extra graph content in normalization or readout.
analysis: Real-node counts are not used as a mask; affine/normalization/readout operations include padded positions. Adding two zero-padded nodes to an unchanged graph changes full-model logits by 0.137769.
result: Synthetic counterexample establishes release sensitivity, not its effect under the authors fixed dataset padding. Corrected model accuracy is untested.
repair: Pass real-node masks; zero padded features after transformations and exclude padding from assignments, pooling and normalization.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: The implemented recurrence differs from the analyzed recurrence
claim: The released recurrence is intended to implement the multiview propagation analyzed in the manuscript.
analysis: Paper specifies fixed initial assignments and separate view states propagated before final fusion. Release recomputes assignments and fuses every layer. Literal Eqs \(5\)-\(6\) also gate the first state twice, while release gates once; release adds normalization operations.
result: Alternative implemented architecture can be legitimate; discrepancy does not identify which private code generated tables.
repair: Choose a canonical recurrence: preserve view states/fixed assignments as written, or revise equations and analyze layer-indexed assignments/fusion. Publish actual run configuration.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.

problems.title: Cross-validation and coverage are not reproduced by the entrypoint
claim: The manuscript describes repeated ten-fold cross-validation for its graph-classification results.
analysis: Entrypoint uses fold \(0\) once rather than looping over ten repetitions of ten-fold CV. With \(188\) graphs, floor-width folds test only \(180\) indices; \(180\)-\(187\) are never tested and excluded from final-fold training.
result: Public reproduction path is incomplete; this does not prove the authors omitted their stated protocol in private scripts.
repair: Use stratified complete outer folds and inner selection; preserve splits/seeds and publish \(100\) outer-fold scores plus repetition summaries.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.

problems.title: The directional-diversity proxy is explicitly distinguished from the formal definition
problems.source_location: Main PDF pp.3-4, Definition 1 Main PDF p.9, Eq 13 and Section 5.3
claim: Directional diversity is compared with the formal diversity definition.
analysis: Authors acknowledge cosine-distance measure does not satisfy Definition 1. Vectors \((1,0)\) and \((2,0)\) have zero cosine distance but unequal magnitude; zero vectors need a convention.
result: The authors acknowledge this proxy limitation. It is a scoped clarification, not a current author error or a newly established anti-collapse guarantee.
problems.impact_rationale: No current-error impact: the source already states that the cosine-distance proxy does not satisfy the formal definition.
problems.existing_correction_status: No paper correction is required for the acknowledged proxy distinction; useful discrimination still requires separate evidence.
